concepts.name: Substitution method
concepts.description: Solve one equation for one variable, then substitute that expression into the other equation.

concepts.name: Elimination method
concepts.description: Multiply the equations so one variable has matching coefficients, then add or subtract to remove it.

concepts.name: Setting up two equations
concepts.description: Assign two variables to the two unknowns, then translate each given fact into one equation.

concepts.name: No solution or infinite solutions
concepts.description: Equations that reduce to a false statement have no solution; equations that reduce to a true statement have infinitely many.

concepts.name: Checking a pair of values
concepts.description: Substitute both values into both original equations to confirm they satisfy each one.

formulas.title: Elimination method
formulas.prompt: How do you eliminate one variable from two equations?
formulas.formula: Multiply each equation so one variable has equal (or opposite) coefficients, then add or subtract the equations
formulas.explanation: Once the coefficients of one variable match, adding or subtracting the equations removes that variable, leaving one equation in one unknown.
formulas.example: 2x + 3y = 12 and 2x + y = 8 → subtract: 2y = 4 → y = 2, then x = 3
formulas.commonMistake: Multiplying only one side of an equation.

formulas.title: Substitution method
formulas.prompt: How do you solve by substitution?
formulas.formula: Solve one equation for one variable; substitute that expression into the other equation
formulas.explanation: This turns two equations in two unknowns into one equation in one unknown.
formulas.example: From x + y = 10, x = 10 − y. Substitute into 2x + y = 16: 2(10 − y) + y = 16 → y = 4, x = 6
formulas.commonMistake: Substituting back into the same equation instead of the other one.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Solve x + y = 10 and 2x + y = 16 by substitution.

formulas.title: Setting up two equations
formulas.prompt: How do you set up simultaneous equations from a word problem?
formulas.formula: Assign a variable to each unknown; write one equation per independent fact given
formulas.explanation: Two unknowns need two independent equations; check that the second equation is not just a repeat of the first.
formulas.example: "Twice the cost of a pen plus a pencil is 25; a pen plus twice a pencil is 20" → 2p + q = 25, p + 2q = 20
formulas.commonMistake: Writing two equations that carry the same information.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Set up equations for two pens and a pencil costing 25.

formulas.title: Consistent, inconsistent, dependent
formulas.prompt: When do two linear equations have no solution or infinitely many?
formulas.formula:
a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2 → no solution
a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 → infinitely many solutions
a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2 → exactly one solution
formulas.explanation: Comparing the ratios of coefficients tells you the type of solution before solving.
formulas.commonMistake: Assuming two equations always have exactly one solution.

formulas.title: Checking a solution pair
formulas.prompt: How do you verify a solution (x, y) to simultaneous equations?
formulas.formula: Substitute x and y into both original equations; both must hold
formulas.explanation: A pair that satisfies only one equation is not the solution to the system.
formulas.example: For x = 3, y = 2: check both 2x + 3y = 12 and 2x + y = 8
formulas.commonMistake: Checking only one of the two equations.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Verify x = 3, y = 2 in 2x + 3y = 12 and 2x + y = 8.

formulas.title: Swapped coefficients: add and subtract
formulas.prompt: The equations are ax + by = p and bx + ay = q. What is the quick way?
formulas.formula:
Add: x + y = (p + q) ÷ (a + b)
Subtract: x − y = (p − q) ÷ (a − b)
formulas.explanation: Adding and subtracting give two very simple equations, which together give x and y at once.
formulas.example: 3x + 2y = 12 and 2x + 3y = 13: x + y = 5 and x − y = −1, so x = 2, y = 3.
formulas.commonMistake: Multiplying to eliminate one variable as usual, which takes three times as long.

formulas.title: Cross-multiplication
formulas.prompt: Is there a formula that gives x and y directly from a₁x + b₁y = c₁ and a₂x + b₂y = c₂?
formulas.formula:
D = a₁b₂ − a₂b₁
x = (c₁b₂ − c₂b₁) ÷ D
y = (a₁c₂ − a₂c₁) ÷ D
formulas.explanation: This is elimination done once in general. D = 0 means the lines are parallel or the same.
formulas.commonMistake: Mixing up the order in the numerators, which flips the sign.

levels.title: Two Unknowns, Two Equations
levels.description: Finding a pair of values that satisfies two equations at once.

blocks.title: Why two equations?
blocks.body: One equation in two unknowns, like x + y = 10, has endless solutions. A second independent equation, like x − y = 4, narrows it down to exactly one pair: x = 7, y = 3.

blocks.title: Elimination
blocks.body: Match coefficients, then add or subtract to remove one variable.
blocks.caption: x + y = 10 and x − y = 4 add to 2x = 14.

blocks.title: Substitution
blocks.body: Solve one equation for one variable, then plug that expression into the other equation, turning two unknowns into one.

questions.question: Solve: x + y = 10, x − y = 4. What is x?
questions.explanation: Add the equations: 2x = 14, so x = 7 (and y = 3).
questions.method: Adding removes y since its coefficients are +1 and −1.

questions.question: Solve: x + y = 10, 2x + y = 16. What is x?
questions.explanation: From the first equation, y = 10 − x. Substitute: 2x + 10 − x = 16, so x + 10 = 16, x = 6.

hints.text: Solve the simpler equation for y first.

commonMistakes: Substituting into the same equation again.

questions.question: To solve for two unknowns, you generally need
questions.explanation: Two unknowns require two independent equations that are not multiples of each other.
questions.method: Match the number of equations to the number of unknowns.

hints.text: Think about how many constraints pin down two values.

questions.question: Solve: 2x + 3y = 12, 2x + y = 8. What is y?
questions.explanation: Subtract the second equation from the first: 2y = 4, so y = 2 (and x = 3).
commonMistakes: Adding instead of subtracting, doubling x.

questions.question: For x = 3, y = 2, does the pair satisfy 2x + 3y = 12 and 2x + y = 8?
commonMistakes: Checking only one equation and assuming the other also holds.

questions.question: Solve: 3x + 2y = 16, 5x − 2y = 8. What is x?
questions.explanation: Add the equations: 8x = 24, so x = 3 (and y = 3.5).

questions.question: Solve: 2x + 3y = 18, 3x + 2y = 17. What is x + y?
questions.explanation: Adding the two equations: 5x + 5y = 35, so x + y = 7.
questions.method: Sometimes adding directly gives the combined value needed.

hints.text: Add the two equations before solving for x and y separately.

commonMistakes: Solving fully for x and y before noticing the shortcut.

questions.question: Two pens and a pencil cost ₹25; a pen and two pencils cost ₹20. What is the cost of one pen?
questions.explanation: Let pen = p, pencil = q: 2p + q = 25, p + 2q = 20. Multiply the second by 2: 2p + 4q = 40. Subtract the first: 3q = 15, q = 5. Then p = 20 − 10 = 10.
questions.method: Set up two equations, then eliminate.

hints.text: Scale one equation so a variable matches.

commonMistakes: Assuming one pen equals one pencil.

questions.question: Solve: 3x − y = 7, 2x + 3y = 1. What is y?
questions.method: Solve one equation for a variable, then substitute.

hints.text: Isolate y from the first equation.

commonMistakes: Sign error when substituting a negative expression.

questions.question: How many solutions does 2x + 3y = 6 and 4x + 6y = 10 have?
questions.explanation: The coefficient ratios 2/4 = 3/6 = 1/2 are equal but 6/10 ≠ 1/2, so the lines are parallel and distinct: no solution.

hints.text: Check if the ratios of x, y and constant terms are equal.

commonMistakes: Assuming two different-looking equations always intersect.

questions.question: A boat travels 30 km upstream in 3 hours and 30 km downstream in 2 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water (in km/hr)?
questions.explanation: Upstream speed = 30/3 = 10 = b − s. Downstream speed = 30/2 = 15 = b + s. Adding: 2b = 25, so b = 12.5 km/hr.
questions.method: Set up boat-speed equations, then eliminate.

hints.text: Speed = distance ÷ time for each leg.

commonMistakes: Averaging the two speeds incorrectly by forgetting to divide by 2 correctly.

questions.question: Solve: 4x + 3y = 25, 3x + 4y = 24. What is x − y?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the equations: x − y = 1. (Solving fully: adding gives 7x + 7y = 49, so x + y = 7; combined with x − y = 1 gives x = 4, y = 3.)
questions.method: Subtracting directly can give the requested combination.

hints.text: You do not need to solve for x and y separately if you only need x − y.

commonMistakes: Solving the full system unnecessarily and making an arithmetic slip.

questions.question: The sum of a two-digit number’s digits is 9. If the digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original. What is the original number?
questions.explanation: Let tens digit = x, units digit = y: x + y = 9. Original = 10x + y; reversed = 10y + x. Reversed − original = 9(y − x) = 27, so y − x = 3. With x + y = 9: y = 6, x = 3. Number = 36.
questions.method: Represent the two-digit number algebraically, then set up two equations.

hints.text: Reversed minus original simplifies to a multiple of (y − x).

commonMistakes: Forgetting the factor of 9 when comparing reversed and original numbers.
